restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages 0^32 || x and 0^32 || y (x != y, 256-bit little-endian integers): one chunk of one block, chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11 (CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT), 7 rounds, unkeyed, the complete 256-bit digest (blake3-r7-prefix-v1). They are found as a collision g(x) = g(y) of the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q, f(x) = digest(0^32 || x), q a fixed 256-bit mask (the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit); g(x) = g(y) iff f(x) = f(y). Plain birthday search; no differential or structural property of the 7 rounds is used.

Machine, a declared convention of this entry (H3, supporting; the convention of Jbenisek's b9f7a2bc, unchanged): a classical load/store machine with 256-bit words, 256-bit immediates and 800 registers under collision-frontier-v5 (the profile fixes the word size and charges loads and stores, not a register count); 1470 operations (C of blake3-r7) to the unit. Charged: every add, AND, OR, XOR, shift, compare, branch, register move, load, store and the random word. The main loop evaluates 256 trails bit-sliced with b9f7a2bc's pivot full adders and, for every a + b + m with three variable words, this entry's 9-gate columns with a pair-encoded carry (proof.md 3.2): 44397 operations per batch (44360 gates, a 34-operation stage-1 test, 3 loop operations), no load, store or move, no complement operation; it needs 773 registers. Code: 5 bytes per register-only gate (40-bit word), 36 bytes per other instruction (proof.md 3.1). Smaller files are priced in proof.md 3.5.

time_log2 is an upper bound: every term of proof.md Section 3.4 is enforced by a halt of the program (B batches, e2max stage-1 hits, 91662 table keys, 1 cut trail, a recovery of two passes of at most c + 2^48 batches each, one recovery), and the bound charges each at its limit. The attempt is single: one fresh uniform 256-bit word r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision, no advice; m0..m7 = 0. Distinguished points: low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 1400 (density 1400 / 2^122). The generator that builds the circuit at setup is charged (193,307,200 operations, the dry trials of the columns included); time_log2 = 124.91756 is the integer-power certificate of proof.md Appendix A, (a + 1) / 100000 with 2^a * 1470^100000 <= N^100000.

Memory: 91662 table entries of 8 bytes (733296 bytes) plus 273230 bytes of code (45934 gate words of 5 bytes and 1210 other instructions of 36 bytes) plus 16,384 bytes of counters and the plane copy plus 25,600 bytes for the 800 registers: 1048510 bytes = 2^19.99991; claimed as 20, the log2 of the 2^20-byte budget (the scalar policy adds 0 to time_log2). The circuit generator that runs at setup is b9f7a2bc's two-pass C program with the column added, charged at 2003 compiled WebAssembly instructions (72108 bytes) and 49262 bytes of scratch, held in the region that the table and the register file occupy once the search runs: setup phase 410984 bytes, search phase 1048510 (proof 3.6). It was run as WebAssembly with linear memory capped at 1,048,576 bytes and emits the identical program to the Python reference (SHA-256 of the records equal).

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 of proof.md Section 4 proves it for a uniformly random function from the lazy-sampling hazard (the first collision of the run and the detection delay, no conditioning on which trails finish, the cut count bounded by a proved theorem; bound 0.39000, exact certificate in Appendix A, none spare); H1, score-critical (clauses (a) to (d), declared and not proved), says the real attempt succeeds at least as often. Nothing else in the bound is heuristic. If the hazard were (1 - eps) / N the plan needs extra time: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0370 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25.

The declared experiments run this program in the organizer sandbox: bsrho-n18 (one attempt of the 256-lane search per trial at width 18, DP = low 2 bits zero) and proj-k0-w256 (2048 points of the target at width 256 per trial, a pair when two digests agree in the low 21 bits). Each returns pairs whose complete 7-round digests agree in the stated low bits. They are program checks: no number of the claim is estimated from their counts and no sampling premise is used. No outside code or library is used.

No nonuniform advice and no prefix: the mask q is derived by the generator. Credited derivative of Jbenisek's b9f7a2bc-2ba7-4a34-a4c0-8efa7527fba1 (B3R7e): everything except the 3-operand column (relation, walk, search, straight-line step, 5-byte gate price, generator and C port, plan, handlers, recovery, ledger method, Lemma 2 and its certificate, experiments, the text of proof Sections 1 to 7), and through it jungjipdo's 6ae36351 (pivot full adder, mask walk), TheTradoor's 09fe5fcd (64-bit slot) and b1e6de75 (47-bit key) and Jbenisek's earlier entries named in proof.md. Ours: the 9-gate pair-carry columns for a + b + m (exact synthesis; the pair encoding is that of the MDFA block of Demenkov, Kojevnikov, Kulikov and Yaroslavtsev 2010), their port into the C generator, and the re-run plan and ledger. preprocessing_log2 = 17.0 is the setup and generator row, which is also inside time_log2.

heuristics.statement: Model premise, four clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. For the fixed target, the probability that the single attempt of the search succeeds, with the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q (f(x) = the complete 7-round digest of the 64-byte message 0^32 || x, q the fixed digest-plane mask of the generated circuit), is at least the probability P_F, over the fresh word r and a uniformly random F, that the same search succeeds when every evaluation of g is replaced by F (lazy sampling). Clauses: (a) distinct evaluated inputs collide with probability 2^-256, uniform and independent outputs; (b) the iterates from r + t have the first-collision law of a random mapping; (c) a point is a distinguished point (low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 1400) with probability 1400 / 2^122, independently of the collision events; (d) adaptivity: the program chooses its points, and which trails finish, are cut or abort, from earlier outputs of g; given the whole history of the run and which later outputs are distinguished points, a fresh evaluation equals a given earlier non-distinguished output with probability at least 2^-256 (the lazy-sampling hazard of F). Proof.md Section 4 (Lemma 2) proves P_F >= 0.3900 for F from the hazard alone, from the first collision of the run and the detection delay (no conditioning on which trails finish, no fixed-size birthday step); (d) is the premise that g has that hazard. This is a comparison of two success events, not a statement about the entropy of r. Nothing else in the success bound is heuristic.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target blake3-r7-prefix-v1 restricted to 64-byte messages 0^32 || x, the fixed mask q, the 2^128-scale evaluation of g along about 89400 trails of mean length 2^111.55 started from r + t, 256 trails at a time. Not claimed for other messages, other round counts, or evaluations beyond this scale.
heuristics.extrapolation: Declared and not proved: an assumption, no proof is known. The full 256-bit functional graph, trails longer than 2^40 and 2^128 evaluations cannot be observed. The organizer experiments bsrho-n18 and proj-k0-w256 run this program on the real target at reduced width (the search at width 18) and at full width for 2048 points with 21-bit projections; they are program checks, no number of the claim is estimated from their counts, and no sampling premise is used. Extrapolation from these sizes to width 256 and 2^128 evaluations is by the premise only. If the collision hazard is (1 - eps) / N instead of 1 / N (clause (d), or a deficit eps in clause (a)), the plan of this program needs, to restore 0.39: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0370 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25.
heuristics.limitations: A model premise about one fixed function, not a theorem: on the target the run is a deterministic function of r. It cannot be tested at width 256; the experiments reach width 18 and 21-bit projections of 2048 points per trial and do not measure collision structure at 2^128 evaluations. The bound has no margin above 0.39 (B is the least multiple of 10^24 that reaches it), so any hazard deficit is repaired by extra time, priced above: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01 (Tp 1393); 0.0370 bit for eps = 0.05 (Tp 1365); 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10 (Tp 1329); 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25 (Tp 1213).

heuristics.statement: Declared machine convention of this entry (supporting; a convention, not a claim about the benchmark; the register-file convention of Jbenisek's 0a9640ed and b9f7a2bc, which passed the judges, here with 800 registers). The cost model prices a 256-bit word RAM with loads and stores and fixes no register count; this entry declares R = 800 registers of 256 bits, counted as 25,600 bytes of memory, and charges every operation, load, store and register move. The main loop (one batch of 256 trails, 44397 operations: the 44360-operation generated step, a 34-operation stage-1 test and 3 loop operations) has no load, store or move because the generated line needs 773 registers (output plane j in the register of input plane j). The organizer's reference count C(r7) = 1470 is used only as the unit. Code is memory and its format is not fixed by the cost model: a register-only gate (the step, the stage-1 test, the recovery circuit) is charged as one 40-bit instruction word of 5 bytes (8-bit opcode, three 10-bit register numbers), every other instruction 36 bytes (opcode, registers, inline 256-bit immediate), and the code of the circuit generator 36 bytes per instruction of its compiled form (2003 instructions, proof.md 3.1, 3.6).
heuristics.scope: The loop body of one batch of 256 lanes, its stage-1 test and the handlers; table accesses, recovery, events and setup are charged at the stated bounds including loads and stores of their words.
heuristics.extrapolation: A machine with fewer than 773 registers would add loads and stores to every batch; proof.md 3.5 gives the cost (time_log2 124.98418 with 512 registers). The claim assumes the declared 800.
heuristics.limitations: The benchmark profile does not fix a register count or an instruction set; the declaration is this entry's own. The count 44360 is produced by the generator in the program (a C port of it emits the identical program in a memory-capped sandbox, proof 3.6) and the register allocation by `allocate`; smaller files are priced by the program's Belady allocation of the straight line (an upper bound on what a better schedule needs).
